items.suggested_text:
A -52% drawdown looks brutal next to gold's -36%, but measured against Bitcoin's own history it sits on the shallow end. The 2011 cycle fell 92.7% and took 622 days to reclaim its high; the 2013 peak fell 84.5% and needed 1,177 days. The drops have tended to get shallower as the asset grew, not deeper.

The comparison also puts two very different markets side by side: gold is a mature asset held by central banks for centuries, while $BTC still carries the volatility of something whose holder base is widening every cycle.

Every cycle's drop and recovery time, mapped: https://x.com/ForecastQuant/status/2122375393776951738

Depth is only half of it. How long the market takes to get back to the high says far more about who is actually holding through it.
